title: Robot Kinematics and Dynamics
learner_summary: The learner is a graduate mechanical engineering student with a solid foundation in classical mechanics and basic robotics concepts.

objectives.text: given a serial arm, assign DH frames and compose the homogeneous transforms to express every joint axis zᵢ and every frame origin Oᵢ in the base frame.
Find the endpoint velocity from the joint rates.
Explain each column of the Jacobian physically.

facts.text: Column formulas. For a rotary joint i, column i is [z_{i-1} x d_{i-1,n}; z_{i-1}]. For a prismatic joint i, it is [z_{i-1}; 0]
Everything is in base-frame coordinates. Both z_{i-1} and d_{i-1,n} = Oₙ - O_{i-1} are written in frame 0, and d runs from joint i's axis to the endpoint, not along a single link.

Jv is not ∂f/∂θ. The top three rows are partial derivatives of the position. The bottom three rows give angular velocity ω, which is not the time derivative of any set of orientation coordinates. The Jacobian with respect to Euler angles is a different matrix, J = C⁻¹Jv

misconceptions.text: The Jacobian is always just the partial derivatives of forward kinematics.
misconceptions.correction: The Jacobian also includes the angular velocity part, which is not captured by the partial derivatives of the position alone.

misconceptions.text: The Jacobian only applies to revolute joints.
misconceptions.correction: The Jacobian applies to both revolute and prismatic joints, with different column formulas for each type.

misconceptions.text: Joint i rotates about zᵢ, and its position is Oᵢ.
misconceptions.correction: Joint i actually rotates about z_{i-1}, and its position is O_{i-1}.
